instructions: Cut the beef into 3/4 inch cubes and pat them dry. Season with 1 teaspoon of the salt, then toss with the flour.
Heat 3 tablespoons of the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in 3 batches, 3 to 4 minutes a batch, until deep golden. Don't crowd the pot. Transfer each batch to a plate.

Turn the heat down to medium. Dice the onions and add them to the pot with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and the cloves. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until the onions are soft.
Return the beef and its juices to the pot. Stir in the cinnamon, allspice and sugar and cook for 1 minute, until you can smell the spices.
Add the wine, turn the heat up, and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until it has reduced by about half.

Add the broth and the passata. Bring to a simmer, then turn the heat down to medium-low and cover, leaving the lid slightly open. Cook for 1 hour 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beef is very tender and the sauce coats the spoon. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
About 15 minutes before it's done, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the bucatini until al dente, then drain.
Stir the vinegar into the stew and take out the cloves. Taste it, and add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt if it's flat.
Divide the bucatini among bowls and spoon the stew over it. Top with the Parmesan. Put the red pepper flakes on the table for the adults.
To keep it, cool the stew and refrigerate it for up to 4 days or freeze it for up to 3 months. Cook fresh bucatini each time. Reheat the stew over low heat with a splash of water.
method_notes: No version has 20 ratings (Krumpli has none, Dimitra's Dishes has none, Culinary Flavors 4.7 from 3, Food.com one review), and RecipeTin Eats has no pastitsada, so this is a fallback led by Krumpli, whose staged method (flour-dusted beef, wine reduced, vinegar at the end) is the most careful. Dimitra's Dishes uses the tomato, cloves and cinnamon without wine; Culinary Flavors adds more spices and mushrooms. Amounts are doubled from Krumpli's version for two. Chili flakes are on the table, not in the pot. It is a long braise but a batch dish that keeps.
